question: Rendering an INR at a coarser grid by point sampling aliases; the correct output is the mean over each output pixel's footprint. For a programmable dictionary the box-footprint program (stage 03, exact for one sine layer; first-order for bounded deep nets) turns prefiltering into a weight edit, after which point sampling IS footprint integration. How much aliasing error does it remove, against the cost-matched alternative of supersampling?

setup.zoos: mnist_shallow64 (L=2, exact program), mnist_s32_swing2 (deep, first-order program), mnist_s32 (standard deep, program expected to fail), 20 networks each
setup.reference: ground-truth footprint mean: render the continuous function at 8x the fine 28-grid (224 samples per side over the domain, uniform spacing), average over the output pixel's footprint for downscale factors 2, 4 and 7 (14, 7 and 4 output pixels per side)

methods.point: evaluate the original network at the output pixel centres (1 sample per output pixel; aliased)
methods.program: edit the weights with box_transfer(c, c) for footprint c = factor pixels of the 28-grid, then evaluate at the centres (1 sample per output pixel)
methods.supersample_k: average k x k point samples per output pixel of the original network, k = 2 and 4 (4 and 16 samples per pixel)
methods.first_order_deep: for deep nets, the program is input_attenuation with the box transfer applied to the first layer's plane waves

setup.metric: PSNR of each method against the ground-truth footprint mean, per network, median over 20; also the relative energy of the aliasing error

predictions_frozen_before_running.AA1_shallow_exact: On the one-sine-layer zoo, program PSNR exceeds 60 dB at every factor (exact up to the reference's own discretisation), while point sampling is below 30 dB at factor 4.
predictions_frozen_before_running.AA2_beats_supersampling: On the one-sine-layer zoo, the program (1 sample per pixel) beats 4 x 4 supersampling (16 samples per pixel) by at least 10 dB at factor 4.
predictions_frozen_before_running.AA3_bounded_deep: On swing-2 deep nets the first-order program improves over point sampling by at least 6 dB at factor 4 and stays within 6 dB of 4 x 4 supersampling.
predictions_frozen_before_running.AA4_standard_deep_fails: On standard deep nets the first-order program does not improve over point sampling by more than 1 dB at factor 4.

why_it_matters: Prefiltered (mip-mapped) rendering of neural fields otherwise needs supersampling or architecture-specific tricks (integrated positional encodings, cone tracing); on a programmable dictionary it is a weight edit computed once per footprint, and anisotropic footprints are the same edit with different (c_y, c_x).
